objective: Repair six evidenced failure modes in the canary job search: initial-request timeout, slow-source isolation, bounded metadata hydration, failed-batch recovery, UI progress and real end-to-end validation.
allowed_changes: Instrument actual request latency before changing time budgets or source behavior
Allow catalog batches to run independently of the initial aggregator and retain all real partial results
Bound and attribute catalog and per-source failures, avoid duplicate expensive retries and preserve consistent pagination
Use only validated country, mode and publication evidence from existing listing and detail APIs
Display accurate search status and per-source quality/latency evidence in the existing UI
Add regression and real-data tests, build the UI and deploy only to the existing isolated canary
forbidden_changes: scoring formula, profile facts, CV generation engine or templates, persistence schema
new services, dependencies, database tables, schedulers or collectors
paid AI calls for unconfirmed eligibility or invalid JD
assuming missing country or work mode implies eligibility
main or production changes, GitHub Actions, Vercel or mock substitutions
acceptance: Failures in initial aggregation do not prevent actual catalog jobs from reaching the UI
Timeouts and skipped batches are visible with source attribution, and recovery does not duplicate jobs
Country, mode, date and history still exclude invalid postings; no mock reaches production
Twenty or more real sampled searches confirm completion behavior and relative latency where authenticated access is available
Every targeted regression fails on the previous canary and passes on the new code
Scope gate, tests, UI build, real canary deployment and end-to-end checks succeed; main stays untouched
deployment: Canary only; no main merge without explicit user approval
